title: upfly optimize --json: the result
description: The last line upfly optimize --json prints when the run finishes: the plan, what an applied run wrote, and the report. Without --apply nothing is written and run is null. Progress and diagnostic lines come before it (events.json); a run that stops or refuses prints an error line instead (events.json).

apply.description: Whether --apply was given, so the plan was written.

only.description: With --only: the images it named, and each pattern that named none. null without --only.

plan.description: What the run converts and rewrites, and what it decided against. The same with and without --apply.

rewrites.description: The references that move, one entry per file.

declined.description: Everything the plan decided against, each with its reason.

line.description: The line, counted from 1, or null when the reason is about a whole file.

keptOriginals.description: Unless originals are kept (--keep-originals, or keep-original in the config), the converted images whose original stays anyway, and why.

refusal.description: Why the plan holds nothing at all, or null. A command that meets one stops with an error line, so its result always has null.

quality.description: The quality the saving was measured at and the file is written at, or "lossless".

replacesOriginal.description: true when the original is removed: by default, unless --keep-originals or the config keeps originals, once every reference to it moves and no file Upfly reads still names it.

edits.description: In the order they appear in the file.

textHash.description: SHA-256 of the file's text as Upfly read it. The edits are made only to a file that still holds that text.

edit.description: One path re-spelled: a reference, or a path inside a comment. The offsets count the file's text in UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript counts a string.

expected.description: The text the edit replaces, the path as written.

inComment.description: The path is inside a comment, which no page loads. It moves with the references, and is never counted as one.

run.description: What an applied run wrote, or null when it wrote nothing: a dry run, or a plan with nothing to do. upfly undo puts every one of these files back.

id.description: The run's id, which the commit message names.

commit.description: The hash of the one commit --commit made, or null.

repository.description: The git repository the project is in, or null when it is in none: top is the repository's folder, and path is the project's folder inside it, empty when they are the same.

notes.description: Things worth knowing about the run, each a sentence: on a dry run, what --apply would refuse, such as uncommitted changes; with --only, how many images it left out.
